item.title: 2nd Friday ArtAbout at the Pence Gallery — Fri Sep 11, 6:00 PM — Pence Gallery
item.description: 2nd Friday ArtAbout at the Pence Gallery Friday, September 11, 6-9 PM (Free) Join us at the Pence Gallery for the opening reception of Art Auction 2026! This spectacular display of art features work by 100+ local & regional artists. Preview sculptures, paintings, photography, textiles, and more on display at the Pence, as well as online for silent auction bidding at bit.ly/penceartauction. Also, enjoy complimentary wine and an art-themed scavenger hunt at the Pence during the 2nd Friday ArtAbout. Complete all of the clues by exploring our exhibit for the chance to win a special prize. The Art Auction is on display from September 5th-26th. Bidding opens online at midnight on Sept. 5th and closes at 8 PM PST on Sept. 26th. — Visit the Pence and other venues in Downtown Davis for the 2nd Friday ArtAbout artwalk. We will have printed ArtAbout guides available that week. Follow the ArtAbout’s Facebook page for more information: https://www.facebook.com/davisartabout. Images: Marsha God

item.title: 2nd Friday ArtAbout reception: Nancy Sloan — Fri Sep 11, 6:00 PM — Logos Books
item.description: California Visions Nancy Sloan oil paintings September 1 to October 3 2nd Friday ArtAbout Reception: September 11, 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. Logos Books, 513 Second Street, Davis, CA, 95616 Sloan paints with oils, acrylics, gouache and watercolors. Her goal is to bring her love of the outdoors to her paintings and her audience. When she is out painting ala plein air in the early morning or late afternoon she tries to capture the elusive nature of morning mists, the sun sparkling on a river or lake, or sunlight dappling through trees. She hopes that viewers will experience brief moments of peace and tranquility from her work. Sloan began painting with watercolors, and discovered her love for landscapes, while attending classes at Cabrillo College in Aptos, CA. Although she has traversed many countries, her primary inspiration continues to be the landscapes of California. Sloan has studied with David Hummer, David Shevlino, Alyssa Monks, John Cosby, Camille Przewodek, Gregory Kondos, Gil

item.title: The Addams Family Musical — Fri Sep 11, 7:30 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
A comical feast that embraces the wackiness in every family, features an original story and a dilemma that’s every father’s nightmare: Wednesday Addams, the ultimate princess of darkness, has grown up and fallen in love with a sweet, smart young man from a respectable family whom her parents have never met. She confides in her father and begs him not to tell her mother. Now, Gomez Addams must do something he’s never done before– keep a secret from his beloved wife, Morticia. Everything will change for the whole family on the fateful night they host a dinner for Wednesday’s “normal” boyfriend and his parents. Recommended for ages 10 and up
Source: The Dirt

item.description:

Sessions alternate between floor yoga and chair yoga (on the 2nd and 4th Tuesday). Stay a bit longer on the last Tuesday of the month and join us for coffee or tea afterward!
Like all our events, this class is free, donations are welcome.

item.title: 2nd Friday ArtAbout – Monthly Downtown Davis Art Walk (Free!) — Fri Nov 13, 9:00 AM — CA
item.description:
Join Davis’s beloved 2nd Friday ArtAbout – a free monthly self-guided artwalk coordinated by the Pence Gallery! Every second Friday, stroll downtown Davis to discover fresh exhibits, opening receptions, live music, hands-on activities, and direct chats with local and regional artists at 10+ galleries, co-ops, and businesses. Support our vibrant arts scene, uncover unique talent and styles, and soak up the lively energy – ideal for friends, families, dates, or solo adventures. Many venues offer complimentary refreshments like wine and snacks. Free – no tickets required!
Runs approximately 5:00–9:00 PM (venue receptions vary—check the monthly guide for specifics). Grab the printed guide (with map & details) the week of at the Pence Gallery or participating spots, or download it at pencegallery.org/events/artabout/.

Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants

item.title: "Working Together to Protect Our Neighbors" Public Outreach Meeting — Thu Sep 10, 6:00 PM — Davis Veterans Memorial Center
item.description:
“Working Together to Protect Our Neighbors” Public Outreach Meeting Each year, the City of Davis Police Accountability Commission organizes a community outreach meeting on a local law enforcement topic. Please join us for “Working Together to Protect Our Neighbors,” an event that will explore the local law enforcement response to immigration issues, on Thursday, Sept. 10, from 6-7:30 p.m. at Veterans Memorial Center (203 E. 14th Street). We have three expert speakers for this event:
Michael Gennaco, The OIR Group, City of Davis Independent Police Auditor, will speak about the legal boundaries and accountability expectations governing local law enforcement when federal immigration enforcement occurs in or near our community Todd Henry, City of Davis Police Chief, will speak about the Davis Police can and cannot do in cases of federal immigration enforcement in Davis. item.title: 9/11 Remembrance Ceremony — Fri Sep 11, 8:30 AM — Fire Station 31
item.description:
9/11 Remembrance Ceremony in Davis
September 11th Remembrance Ceremony Hosted by City of Davis Fire Department Sept. 11, 8:30a Fire Station 31 530 5th Street Information from: City of Davis news alerts The City of Davis Fire Department invites the community to join us on 9/11 at 8:30 a.m. at Fire Station 31 (530 5th Street) for a remembrance ceremony honoring the lives lost on September 11, 2001 and the courage and sacrifice of the first responders who answered the call. This year marks the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks. While a quarter century has passed, we continue to remember the nearly 3,000 people who lost their lives, the families forever changed and the firefighters, law enforcement officers, emergency personnel and everyday people who responded with extraordinary courage. All are welcome to attend and join us as we remember those we lost, honor those who served and reflect on the courage and unity that followed.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Waldorf School's Parent & Child Class — Fri Sep 11, 10:00 AM — Davis Waldorf School
item.description:
The first three years in a child’s life are an amazing time of growth that fill parents and caregivers with awe and wonder. Parent & Child classes are held in a warm and welcoming environment that is carefully arranged for creative play in our Buttercup Preschool room. This program offers the very young child freedom to explore within loving boundaries, and teaches parents/caregivers about Waldorf education’s many benefits. Classes are led by an experienced Early Childhood educator and echo the rhythms of the Waldorf preschool. Additionally, classes offer caregivers a place to connect about child development and parenting techniques. We welcome caregivers of all kinds—parents, grandparents, nannies—to join our sessions!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Healing Movement Practice — Sat Sep 26, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Iama Embodied Community What if you gave yourself permission to slow down, breathe, move, and listen to what your body is telling you?
**Healing Movement** is a trauma-informed, embodied spiritual practice that creates space to gently connect with ourselves through movement, breath, music, mindfulness, and reflection.
Together, we’ll explore movement as a way of noticing and moving through the emotions we carry in our bodies—whether that’s grief, anger, fear, shame, joy, or simply the everyday experiences that can be difficult to put into words.
**No dance experience is required.** This is not a dance class, workout, or performance. There is no right way to move. You’re invited to participate at whatever level feels comfortable for you, with an emphasis on choice, gentleness, and listening to your own body.
